title: Running Time of the Last-True Stripper
statement: The fixed Boolean finite Turing machine computes the following function in time $150(n+1)$ on every Boolean word $x$ of length $n$: if $x$ parses as a self-delimiting pair $(a,v)$ and $v$ has a last true bit, output the encoding of $(a,u)$, where $u$ is the prefix of $v$ strictly before that last true bit; otherwise output the empty word. Here the pair parser reads aligned doubled bits until the separator $01$, and the pair encoding doubles the bits of the first component, appends $01$, and then appends the second component.
